system.name: KPerfIR
system.one_liner: a compiler-centric IR infrastructure that lets performance-profiling tools be composed as compiler passes sharing program semantics and metrics

components.name: Program
components.role: the input AI kernel program in the prior-art profiling flow

components.name: Profiler
components.role: a profiler that observes execution but is disconnected from compiler semantics in prior designs

components.name: Compiler
components.role: the compiler producing dialects/binaries, separate from the profiler in prior designs

components.name: Dialect A
components.role: one compiler IR dialect used in the compilation path

components.name: Dialect B
components.role: another compiler IR dialect used in the compilation path

components.name: Third-party Performance Tool
components.role: an external analysis tool loosely attached to prior profiler output, or exchanging semantics/metrics with KPerfIR's IR

components.name: Performance Insights
components.role: the output produced by the prior profiler flow

components.name: Hardware
components.role: the target hardware (Nvidia, AMD) executing the program

components.name: IR
components.role: KPerfIR's central compiler IR that carries program semantics and profiling metrics together

components.name: KPerfIR Dialects
components.role: dialects defining Operations and Passes for compiler-integrated profiling

components.name: Kernel Program IR
components.role: the kernel-level IR instrumented with profiling operations

components.name: Execution Trace
components.role: the profiling trace produced from running the instrumented binary on hardware

components.name: AI Workloads
components.role: example workloads (Flash Attention, GEMM) profiled through the pipeline

components.name: ① Programmable Tools with IR Semantics
components.role: example novel tool: a loop-profiling tool built with IR-level semantics

components.name: ② Profiling-driven Compiler Passes
components.role: example novel tool: a region-based profiling tool implemented as a compiler pass

components.name: ③ Reusable Performance Tools
components.role: example novel tool: performance tools reused across multiple IR levels (Triton, LLVM, KPerfIR) and hardware backends

flows.to: ① Programmable Tools with IR Semantics

content.key_idea: Unlike prior profilers that sit outside the compiler and lose semantic information, KPerfIR places a shared IR at the center so that profiling operations become first-class compiler passes, enabling programmable, profiling-driven, and reusable performance tools.
content.reading_order: Left to right: prior-art profiler pipeline (Left, showing the disconnect between profiler and compiler), then the KPerfIR compiler-centric concept (middle), then an Enables arrow into three numbered example tools built on top of it (Right).

summary: This wide, two-column concept figure introduces KPerfIR, a compiler-centric infrastructure for GPU kernel performance tooling. The left side compares prior profiler designs, where a Program is profiled externally by a Profiler disconnected from the Compiler's dialects and target Hardware (Nvidia, AMD), against KPerfIR's design, where a shared IR sits at the center, exposing KPerfIR Dialects (Operations, Passes) and exchanging semantics and metrics with third-party performance tools, then lowering to a Kernel Program IR that is executed on hardware to produce an Execution Trace. An Enables arrow on the right fans out to three numbered example tools illustrating the benefits: ① Programmable Tools with IR Semantics (e.g., a loop-profiling tool), ② Profiling-driven Compiler Passes (e.g., a region-based profiling tool), and ③ Reusable Performance Tools spanning multiple IR levels (Triton, LLVM, KPerfIR) and hardware backends. The figure is a dense, small-font conceptual architecture diagram using red/blue/pink/yellow flat-filled rounded boxes with curved arrows and dashed grouping boundaries.
summary_zh: 该图对比了传统性能剖析工具与 KPerfIR 的设计理念：左侧展示传统剖析器与编译器、方言、硬件相互脱节的流程；中间展示 KPerfIR 以共享 IR 为核心，连接方言、第三方工具与硬件；右侧通过“Enables”箭头展示三种由此实现的新型工具（可编程工具、剖析驱动的编译器 pass、可复用工具）。
notes: Figure is very dense with small text (down to 3pt); some component labels (e.g. exact wording inside the three numbered example boxes, code snippet identifiers) are inferred from the visible image and caption rather than from detailed body text, since only one introductory sentence referencing the figure was available.
